cause.R1-005: deliverOutbox and recoverLocalWorkflows reserved up to ten durable rows before executing them sequentially. Only the active row was heartbeated, so a waiting row could lose its lease, be reclaimed and terminally failed, and then still have its provider effect or workflow start invoked by the original worker.

deliverOutbox: Claims exactly one row as execution capacity becomes available, up to the caller's existing bounded limit.
Passes IDs already attempted in the sweep to claimOutbox, so a retryable failure is attempted at most once in that sweep while other eligible work continues.

Renews and verifies the lease immediately before provider delivery. A false renewal or renewal error starts no provider effect, writes no retry projection, and stops the sweep after any in-flight operation returns.
recoverLocalWorkflows: Claims exactly one dispatch as capacity becomes available, retaining the bounded caller limit and leaving suspended dispatch behavior unchanged.

Renews after lookup/createRun but before the workflowRunId projection, then renews again immediately before start/restart. A revoked lease therefore creates neither that projection nor a workflow start.

A lost heartbeat suppresses later terminal projections and ends the sweep. No Run.cancel() is used: Mastra cancellation is not fenced by this application lease and could cancel a new owner's shared run ID.
caseStore: claimOutbox accepts an optional explicit exclusion list and applies it to its eligible-row query; existing callers retain the same behavior.

regressions.name: slow first delivery / terminal second delivery
regressions.proof: Real SQLite and LocalRuntime: while the first local delivery is blocked, the second row remains pending with zero attempts. A competing worker claims it and receives a permanent 400, producing failed/receipt-null/public deliveryStatus=failed. Releasing the old worker cannot create a local receipt for the terminal second row.

regressions.name: bounded retry sweep
regressions.proof: Two retryable 500 rows with a limit of two each receive exactly one attempt; both remain pending and the sweep processes both rather than exhausting one row.

regressions.name: recovery capacity and revoked ownership
regressions.proof: Real SQLite dispatches leave the second pending while the first start waits, permitting another worker to start it. A lookup-time lease-token replacement prevents both workflowRunId projection and start.

base_reproduction_note: The published SHA's confirmed reproduction preclaimed the second row and later delivered it after terminal failure. The new regression asserts the prerequisite property directly: the second row remains pending while the first effect is blocked. That assertion fails against the published implementation because it calls claimOutbox(limit) before the loop. It deliberately does not pin the old reproduction's synthetic claim count, because the durable safety property is lack of early ownership, not a particular schedule used to exhaust attempts.

evidence.result: passed: 1 file, 34 tests, including real SQLite/local-provider lease-batch, retry-bound, recovery-capacity, revoked-ownership, and loopback TCP coverage.

limitations: A lease can still be lost during an already-started external call; durable idempotency and fenced completion remain the recovery boundary. This fix prevents a worker from beginning a queued effect or workflow start after ownership is known lost.
No configuration, state, findings, gates, specs, dependencies, commit, push, or merge status was changed. Findings remain pending independent review.
guarded_regression: Just-in-time looping must exclude retryable items already attempted in the same sweep; the old batch loop did not retry an item multiple times within one sweep.
